newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rally on soft payrolls report.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rally on soft payrolls report.

text.p: Stocks moved further into record territory Friday, with the S&P 500 index topping 700 points for the first time, after a shockingly weak September payrolls report calmed inflation fears and triggered furious buying in the bond market.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 43.24 points to 5,976.09, after climbing 50 points earlier, and was well above Wednesday's record of 5,933.97.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks jumped 7.39 points to 700.17, topping 700 for the first time.

"From the market's perspective, the (payrolls) report seemed to validate the soft-landing school of thought," said Michael Metz, Oppenheimer & Co chief investment strategist, referring to the economic scenario in which growth slows to a more moderate, sustainable pace.

The September employment data included an unexpected 40,000 decline in non-farm payrolls. Economists had expected non-farm payrolls growth to slow in the month, but even so had called for about 166,000 jobs to be added.
Bonds surged on the figure, which confirmed a slowing of the economy and dispelled some of the worst fears about the near-term prospect of inflation.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond surged more than a full point, pushing the yield down to the psychologically key 6.75 percent level from 6.84 percent at Thursday's close.
The stock market rally was less dramatic, and analysts noted the news was actually a mixed blessing for equities.
"You can't get away from the possibility that in a slowing economy, earnings will also slow," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.
A weak earnings report at one Dow component, Aluminum Co. of America, pulled the average well off its highs.

Alcoa reported earnings that were well short of analysts' estimates. The stock was halted ahead of the earnings release and upon resuming trade, Alcoa slumped 3 to 57-1/2, dragging the Dow industrials lower with it.

Concern about upcoming earnings has tended to undermine the stock market's ability to participate in bond market rallies the way it had earlier in the year, and analysts said a severe slowing of the economy would only intensify worries.
"You're already seeing a dramatic slowdown in the rate of earnings growth," Metz said, "and I believe we're going to see more pressure on corporate profits in 1997."
The increasingly favourable interest rate environment was greeted enthusiastically in the rate-sensitive financial sector, which saw stock prices surge.
Wells Fargo & Co. soared 5-3/8 to 266-3/8, BankAmerica Corp. jumped 2 to 86-1/2, Bankers Trust New York Corp. gained 1-3/4 to 81-5/8 and Morgan Stanley Group Inc. climbed 1-3/8 to 51-1/2.
Among individual issues, Stratus Computer Inc. jumped 2-3/4 to 22-1/2 after Salomon Brothers upgraded the shares to strong buy.
Raytheon Co. tumbled 4-1/8 to 48-7/8 after warning its third-quarter operating income would be about 15 percent lower than year-ago levels.
Redhook Ale slid 4-5/16 to 16-3/4 after Smith Barney downgraded the shares to neutral from outperform.
